title: Reconcile confirmation dispatch after the Cloud Run migration
telemetry: Supplied Cloud Run console service and job details, Cloud Logging request and application records for cloud_run_revision and cloud_run_job, and a sanitized counterparty-gateway owner acknowledgment export; no live Cloud Logging, console or gateway access.
owner: Noor, Confirmations on-call, owns the investigation; the application owner owns the dispatch worker, billing and job retry settings; the counterparty-gateway owner owns acknowledgment records and any correction or resend. ITO coordinates the existing TLC.
task: Noor has asked for a bounded investigation after the confirmation reconciliation for booking batch B-2290 failed following the 6.0.0 Cloud Run migration release. Review the supplied console observations and return an evidence-grounded technical update for the existing TLC: which dispatch path owned the batch, what the records support, remaining unknowns, and the next useful check with its owner. No resend, re-run, configuration or billing change is authorized.
common_evidence:
All projects, services, jobs, instances, people, trades and business events in this historical packet are synthetic; no real confirmation was sent.
Window: 2026-10-14T14:00:00Z through 2026-10-14T14:32:00Z; task received at 14:32:00Z.
Scope: project synthetic-confirms-prod; region us-east1; Cloud Run service confirm-dispatch and Cloud Run job confirm-dispatch-sweep.
Interface: supplied console observations only; no candidate CLI, browser session, direct API access or live production read is available.
ITO's existing TLC is coordinating the incident; Noor joined it at 14:31:00Z.
13:30:00Z release 6.0.0 moved trade-confirmation dispatch from the PCF app to Cloud Run; it created serving revision confirm-dispatch-00021-qex (100% service traffic since 13:31:00Z) and job confirm-dispatch-sweep.
Service configuration viewed 14:25:00Z (Scaling tab): billing setting request-based; minimum instances 0; maximum instances 10; maximum concurrent requests 80; request timeout 300s.
Job configuration viewed 14:25:00Z (Task capacity): tasks 4; parallelism 4; maximum retries per task 3; task timeout 10m; an existing schedule creates an execution every 15 minutes.
Application owner's 6.0.0 design note (supplied text, not code): POST /batches records a batch and returns 202. If the gateway rate-limit signal is clear at acceptance, a background worker in the accepting service instance claims the batch and sends its confirmations after the response. If the signal is set, the batch is marked for the sweep job instead. Each confirmation is owned by exactly one path; the sweep sends only sweep-marked confirmations. Each sweep task takes the partition selected by its task index, sends every confirmation in it, then records sent marks for the whole partition at the end.
The design note states no idempotency key or deduplication at the counterparty gateway.
Historical baseline: on PCF, 2026-10-05 through 2026-10-12, the same reconciliation matched every batch (112 batches); this predates the Cloud Run release and is not a current measurement.
14:31:00Z reconciliation report for booking batch B-2290 (40 trades, submitted 14:02:00Z), covering gateway acknowledgments through 14:30:00Z: status=MISMATCH; 6 of 40 trades out of reconciliation. The summary does not say whether those trades lack an acknowledgment or have more than one.
B-2290 is the only batch in this report; post-release batches before 14:00:00Z and after B-2290 are not covered.
The packet contains no resend, re-run, configuration change or correction receipt, and no counterparty statement of impact.

sources.claim: Cloud Run services use request-based billing by default, under which CPU is allocated only during request processing; instance-based billing is the alternative for short-lived background tasks. The settings were previously called 'CPU only allocated during request processing' and 'CPU always allocated'. The billing setting appears on the service's Scaling tab. All Cloud Run jobs use instance-based billing, so the setting does not govern the sweep job.

Background activity is anything after the HTTP response is delivered; under request-based billing the instance's CPU access is disabled or severely limited after a request finishes, so Google advises against background threads outside request handlers. Google does not quantify the remaining CPU, so the case depends only on progress coinciding with request intervals, not on a rate.
Maximum retries is the number of times a task may restart after failure; it applies per task, not per job, defaults to 3 and accepts 0 to 10. With 0, tasks run once and are not retried.

Google advises making jobs idempotent so a task restart does not produce corrupt or duplicate output, avoiding duplicates by reusing a unique identifier or checking whether output exists, and checkpointing progress. The fixture's end-of-partition sent marks and gateway acceptance of both copies are authored application behavior, not provider behavior.

A Task records its index, a retried count of retries up to maxRetries, and lastAttemptResult with status and exit code. The console Tasks tab exists but Google does not document its display wording, so the fixture states retried counts and attempt results rather than console text.

Service logs use cloud_run_revision and job logs use cloud_run_job, whose entries carry execution_name, task_index and task_attempt labels. Whether attempt numbering starts at 0 or 1 differs in wording between this page and the container contract's CLOUD_RUN_TASK_ATTEMPT, so the case names first and second attempts instead. Application record text is synthetic.

a.conclusion: B-2290 was owned by the post-response worker on instance 0c71d4e9. Its sending advanced only just after the 202 and during the two later intervals when that instance served requests, and 6 confirmations remain claimed and unsent with no error, exit or shutdown recorded. That fits the declared request-based billing, under which CPU is allocated only during request processing. No sweep task touched B-2290 and no task retried; the gateway shows missing, not duplicated, confirmations. Whether the remaining work will finish, and which lifecycle design should replace it, are not established.
next_checks: Application owner confirms whether instance 0c71d4e9 still holds the claim on the 6 confirmations before anyone resends or re-marks them, because a resend while the worker still owns them can duplicate effects.
Counterparty-gateway owner confirms current per-trade acknowledgment state for the 6 outstanding trades and owns any approved resend.

Application owner checks other post-release batches accepted with a clear rate-limit signal for the same stalled pattern and assesses the lifecycle design (finish work before the response, instance-based billing, or the sweep path) as an owner decision.
Noor reports 6 confirmations outstanding and not duplicated on the existing TLC.
unsupported: Blame job retries or duplicate confirmations for the mismatch.
Recommend switching to instance-based billing, or any other billing or retry setting change, as the confirmed fix without an application-owner decision.
Resend, re-mark for the sweep or re-run anything for the 6 confirmations without checking the worker's claim and the gateway state.

unknowns: Whether 0c71d4e9 still exists and will finish the 6 confirmations, or would lose them on idle shutdown.
Outcomes of B-2291 and other batches since 13:30 UTC.
Counterparty impact of the delayed or missing confirmations.

b.conclusion: B-2290 was marked for the sweep job at acceptance and never used the post-response worker. In execution 7kq2m, task 2's first attempt sent 6 confirmations and failed on the 7th, before the end-of-partition sent-mark write; the automatic retry re-sent its whole partition, and the gateway accepted both copies for those 6 trades. A retried, non-idempotent task explains the 6 duplicated confirmations. Request-based billing is declared but does not explain B-2290, and one execution with one task per partition is not proof of single effects.
next_checks: Counterparty-gateway owner identifies the 6 duplicated confirmations by message id and decides any counterparty correction.
Application owner reviews per-confirmation sent marks or an idempotency key for the sweep and decides any retry-setting change.
Application owner checks other executions since 13:30 UTC for tasks with retried greater than 0 and investigates the state-store read timeout.
Noor keeps re-runs and resends on hold until effects are reconciled and reports 6 duplicated confirmations on the existing TLC.
unsupported: Blame request-based billing or recommend switching to instance-based billing as the fix.
Recommend setting maximum retries to 0 as the fix without an owner decision; that would leave a failed partition unsent rather than make the task idempotent.
Re-run the execution or resend confirmations without checking gateway effects.
Claim the gateway deduplicated the copies, or that one execution or one task per partition guarantees single effects.
State the cause of the state-store timeout or the counterparty impact.
unknowns: Why the state-store read timed out.
Whether the counterparty acted on both copies of the 6 confirmations.
Whether other executions since 13:30 UTC retried tasks with the same effect, and whether the post-response path has a separate exposure.
